issues.description: The problem statement's UML and textual description specify acceptSupplyDelivery with four parameters (supplier name, ingredient name, price, quantity) — e.g., acceptSupplyDelivery(String, String, int, int) — but both the template/usage (Main) and the solution implement and call a three-parameter version (ingredient name, price, quantity). This discrepancy will confuse students about the correct method signature to implement (and tests or starter code may expect the 3-arg version).
issues.suggested_fix: Unify the acceptSupplyDelivery signature across artifacts. Either (A) update the problem statement (UML and text) to describe the three-parameter signature acceptSupplyDelivery(String ingredientName, int price, int quantity) to match the template and solution and the provided Main usage, or (B) change the template and solution to implement acceptSupplyDelivery(String supplierName, String ingredientName, int price, int quantity) and update Main accordingly. Prefer option A if the supplier name is not used by exercises/tests.

issues.description: The problem UML does not indicate that the SealSaloon.stock attribute is static, while the textual instructions explicitly require the stock attribute to be static and the solution implements it as static. The UML vs. textual/in-code mismatch could confuse students about whether stock should be an instance or shared (static) attribute.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the UML and textual instructions consistent: either mark the stock attribute as static in the UML (to match the textual requirement and the solution), or if the shared/static behavior is not intended, update the text and solution to use an instance (non-static) stock. Prefer updating the UML to indicate the attribute is static so all artifacts align.

issues.description: The problem statement (UML and text) specifies acceptSupplyDelivery should take four parameters (supplier name, ingredient name, price, quantity) — signature shown as acceptSupplyDelivery(String, String, int, int). The solution implements acceptSupplyDelivery with only three parameters: acceptSupplyDelivery(String name, int price, int quantity). The single String parameter in the solution (named "name") is used as the ingredient name, and there is no parameter for the supplier name. This mismatch in parameter count and meaning can confuse students: they will expect to pass both a supplier name and an ingredient name per the problem description but find only one String parameter in the solution/template, making it unclear which name is intended and whether the supplier is required.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the method signatures consistent. Either update the solution to accept four parameters (String supplierName, String ingredientName, int price, int quantity) and use/store/ignore the supplierName as appropriate, or update the problem statement/UML to require only three parameters (ingredientName, price, quantity) and clarify that supplier name is not needed. Use clear parameter names (supplierName, ingredientName) so students can unambiguously map problem requirements to the implementation.
